book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Not necessarily what you want when sacked by Midas?

definitions.meaning: reads as a warning about an unwelcome gesture, but points to a payoff given to a departing executive
Midas turned everything he touched to gold, so shaking hands with him on dismissal would gild the hand

explanation.surface: A rueful thought about being fired by the mythical king whose touch turned things to gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The parting payment to a sacked executive is called a golden handshake; with Midas, the handshake would literally be golden.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for a generous severance payment given on dismissal or retirement.

clue.text: Criminal bumping off new man who's cracking?

indicators.note: a gangster's own slang for killing, here it means getting rid of one letter from the criminal

parts.note: a gangster is a violent criminal in an organised gang

explanation.surface: A villain murders a newcomer — perhaps a safecracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' suggests a safebreaker, the natural partner of a criminal, but the cracking is of jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is an informal word for a comedian, someone who tells gags or cracks jokes.

clue.text: Reveal leasehold opportunity?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to disclose a secret
second meaning: a property ... a lease, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second reading, a property offered for letting.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is the informal idiom for divulging something, and a building can be let on a lease.

clue.text: Chess move — neat manoeuvring will capture knight and pawn, stupid!

indicators.note: chess language for taking a piece, here meaning the reworked letters close around the others
the letters of neat are moved about, as pieces are manoeuvred on a board

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be manoeuvred
N is the chess notation for a knight
an ass is a stupid person

explanation.surface: Chess commentary: a tidy manoeuvre will win a knight and a pawn, and how foolish of the opponent!
explanation.walkthrough: ASS is a noun meaning a fool, standing in for the adjective stupid as is common in clues.
explanation.definitionFit: En passant is the special chess rule letting a pawn capture an adjacent pawn that has just advanced two squares.

clue.text: Start a car — with rope, possibly, having lost power

indicators.note: signals that the remaining letters could be arranged another way
the fodder is missing one letter, which is the power symbol

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Starting a car by towing it with a rope, maybe, once the engine has no power.
explanation.walkthrough: A tow-rope start sounds plausible for a dead engine, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To hot-wire a vehicle is to bypass its ignition switch to get the engine running without a key.

clue.text: Water initially flowed up — almost 50% whale appearing

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards, so this pair is reversed
takes only the opening letter of water

parts.note: only its opening letter is used
water ran, or flowed

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: half is fifty per cent

explanation.surface: Spray shoots upward as a whale breaks the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic toothed whale, the male having a long spiral tusk.

clue.text: Joins together to lift ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, the last letter is raised to the top of the word

parts.note: loops fasten one thing to another with a loop

explanation.surface: Things connect to hoist a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of the verb is lifted to the front, a move that works because the entry reads downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing vessel, so a type of ship.

clue.text: Maiden under threat and chased by city attorney

parts.note: taken as written
Rome is the Italian capital
DA is a US district attorney

explanation.surface: A girl in danger is pursued by a city lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chased by' means followed by in the answer; the word and is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda was a princess chained to a rock as a sacrifice to a sea monster until Perseus rescued her.

clue.text: Problems are mounting for Dutch scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems
taken as written

explanation.surface: Difficulties pile up for an academic from the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Renaissance humanist thinker and theologian.

clue.text: Received nothing before drug bust?

definitions.note: a verb meaning to fail or collapse, matching the phrasal verb

parts.note: got means received
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone was handed nothing just before a police drugs raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug bust' looks like a police raid; bust is in fact the definition, ruin or decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating or falling into ruin.

clue.text: Runs a Japanese car, taking in day in part of Wales

indicators.note: the car name surrounds the abbreviation for day

parts.note: Honda is a Japanese car maker

explanation.surface: A driver takes a Japanese car on a day trip through Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda is a former coal-mining valley region of South Wales.

clue.text: Composer: "I must work with the note"

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be reworked
taken as written
n. is the standard abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote

explanation.surface: A songwriter's resolution to get on with a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunesmith is an informal word for a writer of tunes, especially popular songs.

clue.text: One participates in concert accepting various skill levels

definitions.note: an adjectival definition, matching the answer used before a noun such as tournament

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the concert

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the London Proms
A means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: A player joins a concert open to musicians of all abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-am competition is open to both professionals and amateurs playing together.

clue.text: Bones: anger about pre-Christian date?

indicators.note: the word for anger is placed around the date

parts.note: rage is fury
1 BC is a year before the Christian era began

explanation.surface: An irritated query over whether some bones date from before Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribcage is the set of rib bones enclosing the chest.

clue.text: It may supply weapon with nasty iron blade

indicators.note: a nasty mess of letters, to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that hands out a weapon with a vicious metal edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a shoulder belt with pockets for cartridges, feeding a soldier's gun with ammunition.

clue.text: Follows advice: tip leads to ease and not squalor

parts.note: to tip is to lean over, or list

indicators.note: the leads of the following words are their opening letters, one from each

parts.note: its opening letter follows the word for tip
its opening letter comes next
its opening letter ends the answer

explanation.surface: Taking a household tip so as to live in comfort, not filth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a piece of advice, but it is a verb meaning tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who listens pays heed to advice and acts on it.

clue.text: Country Romanians wrecked

indicators.note: the word is broken up and its letters rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A nation ruined by people from Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic enclosed by Italy.

clue.text: Medicine and wound-dressing surrounding cold American

indicators.note: the dressing goes around the letter for cold

parts.note: lint is soft fabric used to dress wounds

explanation.surface: A first-aid kit of medicine and bandages wrapped round a chilly American.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a syrupy cough medicine.

clue.text: Long lecture applied to hair disease

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair
a jaw is a long talk or telling-off

explanation.surface: A long talk about a scalp complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair disease' reads as one phrase, but hair belongs to the wordplay and disease stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is the common name for tetanus, a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: Party? Cut of meat's mine

parts.note: shin is a cut of beef from the lower leg
to dig is to mine

explanation.surface: A guest at a party claims a cut of meat as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a possessive, but it is the verb to excavate.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Sweet and doting when meeting soldier

parts.note: fond means loving to excess
a soldier is a caste of ant

explanation.surface: A sugary, devoted person falls for a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft creamy confection or icing made from sugar.

clue.text: Flower: such, if trained, will go over rear of pergola

indicators.note: in a down clue the reshaped letters sit above the final letter
like a climber trained on a frame, these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, the rest of the anagram fodder

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: such a plant, trained, will climb over the back of a pergola.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a shrub with drooping bell-shaped flowers, often grown up supports.

clue.text: Drink supplier still upset about a youth

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the rest
in a down clue, turned upside down means read upwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
taken as written
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A distiller's still is knocked over by a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' suggests distilling, but it is the adverb. A tea lady is the woman who serves tea in British offices.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea lady brings cups of tea round a workplace, so she provides drinks.

clue.text: Run out during tournament — infection?

indicators.note: the dismissal sits within the tournament

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A batsman is dismissed in a competition and wonders if he is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Croup is a respiratory illness in children, usually viral, causing a barking cough.

clue.text: The little angels fixed it up

parts.note: to put is to place or fix

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Children praised for repairing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little angels' reads as well-behaved children; it is the art term.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby winged infants of Renaissance painting, cherubs in art.

clue.text: Blood disorder — a setback for me in Italian island

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the island

parts.note: Ischia is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples
taken as written

indicators.note: the word is set backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laments a health setback while holidaying on an Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischaemia is an inadequate supply of blood to an organ or tissue.

clue.text: I travel abroad, turning up indigenous people

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
to roam is to wander widely

explanation.surface: A traveller overseas meets native people.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'I' was lost from the page scan; the wordplay needs it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian native population of New Zealand.

clue.text: Judge indicated removing prisoner's head in segments

indicators.note: a letter is taken away from the word for indicated

parts.note: pointed means indicated

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A judge pointed at the prisoner, then had his head removed in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jointed has articulated sections connected by joints.

clue.text: Australian, after confused time, going to a philosopher

indicators.note: the Australian follows the confused time

parts.note: a spin is a short spell, and to be in a spin is to be confused
Oz is slang for Australia
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian, after a bewildering spell, visits a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was the seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker.

clue.text: It's not the unemployed keeping the Government in power?

definitions.meaning: people with jobs are 'working', the opposite of unemployed
a parliamentary majority large enough to pass legislation

explanation.surface: A political observation that the jobless are not what keeps a government afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the political term literally as a majority of people in work.
explanation.definitionFit: A working majority is a parliamentary margin big enough for a government to rule effectively.
